draft.title: Approaches to bioethics
card: judges an action by its outcomes. The right choice is the one that gives the best overall result, such as the most good for the most people.
judges an action by whether it follows moral rules or duties, such as telling the truth or not harming others. Outcomes do not decide it.
asks what a person of good character would do, such as someone who is honest, fair and caring.
The same issue can be weighed in all three ways. Each approach asks a different question, so they can lead to different answers.
draft.remember: Outcomes, rules or character: each approach asks a different question about the same issue.

a.q: A scientist says a trial is right because it will probably save many lives. Which approach is this?
opts: Consequences-based, as it judges by the outcome
Duty-based, as it judges by the outcome
Virtue-based, as it judges by the outcome
Duty-based, as it follows a moral rule
a.why: The scientist judges the trial by its likely result, which is lives saved. That is a consequences-based approach. A duty-based approach would ask whether the trial follows moral rules, whatever the outcome.
a.clue: What is the scientist using to decide: outcome, rule or character?

b.q: Dr Lee refuses to hide a risk of a new treatment from patients, even though telling them may cut the number who join the study. She says patients have a right to the truth. Which approach is she using?
opts: Duty-based, as she follows a rule of honesty
Consequences-based, as she wants the best outcome
Virtue-based, as she wants to be seen as honest
Consequences-based, as she expects fewer joiners
b.why: Dr Lee follows a rule that patients must be told the truth, even when this may lead to a worse result for the study. That is duty-based. The tempting option is consequences-based, but she is ignoring the outcome and putting the rule first.
b.clue: She sticks to the rule even when the result may be worse.

a.best: Consequences-based, as it judges by the outcome

b.best: Duty-based, as she follows a rule of honesty
